title_en: Zheng Taifa v. Land Administration Authority — dispute over administrative penalty for land management
keywords_en: administrative; administrative penalty for land management; second instance; intermediate people's court; Sichuan Province; natural person; Land Administration Law; building on farmland without approval; legality of administrative penalty; upholding the original judgment; building on farmland; administrative penalty; illegal construction
full_text_en:
Zheng Taifa v. Changshou County Urban and Rural Construction Committee — dispute over administrative penalty for land management

Plaintiff: Zheng Taifa, male, 35 years old, a farmer of Limin Village, Yuntai Township, Changshou County, Sichuan Province.

Defendant: Changshou County Urban and Rural Construction Committee, Sichuan Province.
Legal Representative: Ran Kaixiang, Director of Changshou County Urban and Rural Construction Committee.
Agent ad litem: Zheng Jintang, specially invited lawyer of Changshou County Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Chen Zhihe, lawyer of Changshou County Law Firm.
Agent ad litem: Li Xiaorong, part-time legal worker of Changshou County Law Firm.

In the case of plaintiff Zheng Taifa's不服 the administrative penalty imposed by Changshou County Urban and Rural Construction Committee, he filed a lawsuit with the Changshou County People's Court. The court formed a collegial panel according to law and, after a public hearing, found the following facts:

The plaintiff Zheng Taifa's family of five originally resided in Group 4 of Limin Village, Yuntai Township, with a 74-square-meter brick-and-wood structured tile-roofed house. In March 1987, on the grounds that "the two brothers' families had increased in number and could not live together, and the original house was transferred to the brother Zheng Heqing for use," Zheng Taifa applied to occupy 180 square meters of his contracted cultivated land to build four rooms in a two-story house (one floor and one basement). After the village group signed off, the application was reported to the Yuntai Township Government. The township government did not approve because the parcel of land for which Zheng Taifa applied was not a planned point for rural housing construction. Without review and approval by the land administration department and without obtaining a building permit, Zheng Taifa arbitrarily commenced construction of a house on the contracted cultivated land. During the construction process, township government staff went to the site multiple times to stop him, but Zheng Taifa ignored them. Subsequently, during the intervention, township government staff confiscated some construction tools, and on October 15, 1987, the township government issued a "Notice of Illegal Construction" to Zheng Taifa, ordering him to demolish the completed project and restore the land for farming within 10 days. Far from complying, Zheng Taifa forcibly accelerated the construction. By November 1987, he had completed a brick-and-concrete structured, three-story (two floors and one basement) house of five rooms with front and rear balconies and an exterior fully decorated with mosaics, totaling 464.1 square meters and occupying 227.2 square meters of cultivated land. In response, on December 20, 1987, the Yuntai Township Government submitted a "Report on the Handling of Zheng Taifa's Forcible Occupation of High-Quality Farmland to Build a House" to the Changshou County Urban and Rural Construction Committee. After investigation and verification, the Changshou County Urban and Rural Construction Committee found that Zheng Taifa's擅自 building a house on cultivated land violated Article 38, paragraph 1, of the Land Administration Law of the PRC, which provides that for rural residents building houses, "if cultivated land is used, the application shall be subject to review by the people's government at the township level and approval by the people's government at the county level." On September 2, 1988, the Committee issued a penalty decision ordering Zheng Taifa to demolish the house built on the cultivated land. Dissatisfied, Zheng Taifa filed a lawsuit with the Changshou County People's Court on the grounds that "my house building was discussed and approved by the masses."

After accepting the case according to law, the Changshou County People's Court, upon trial, found: For building a house on cultivated land, Zheng Taifa should have, in accordance with Article 21 of the Implementation Measures of Sichuan Province for Land Administration, regarding rural residents building houses, first submitted an application by himself, obtained consent from the township people's government, obtained permission from the village and town planning department, undergone review by the land administration department, and reported to the county people's government for approval. However, without approval from the county people's government and without obtaining a building permit, Zheng Taifa illegally built a house on cultivated land. During the construction period, although relevant staff of the township government repeatedly went to the site to advise and stop him and issued a "Notice of Illegal Construction" ordering the demolition of the house under construction and restoration of the land for farming, Zheng Taifa forcibly continued construction and completed the house. His conduct violated Article 38, paragraph 1, of the Land Administration Law. The penalty decision of Changshou County Urban and Rural Construction Committee was correct. In accordance with Article 45 of the Land Administration Law, which provides: "If a rural resident unlawfully occupies land to build a house without approval or by fraudulent means to obtain approval, the illegally occupied land shall be ordered to be returned, and the newly built house on the illegally occupied land shall be ordered to be demolished within a time limit or confiscated," on November 27, 1988, the court rendered judgment: upholding the penalty decision of Changshou County Urban and Rural Construction Committee ordering the demolition of the house built by Zheng Taifa on the illegally occupied cultivated land.

Dissatisfied with the judgment of the Changshou County People's Court, Zheng Taifa appealed to the Chongqing Intermediate People's Court on the grounds that "township government staff verbally agreed to the house building." The court, upon trial, found: The court of first instance, in this case of Zheng Taifa's不服 the administrative penalty for land management, had clearly ascertained the facts, sufficient evidence, correct application of law, and legal procedures. Although township government staff verbally agreed to the house building, Zheng Taifa commenced construction without obtaining approval from the competent approving authority and a building permit, which violated the Land Administration Law; his grounds for appeal cannot stand. Accordingly, on January 10, 1989, in accordance with Article 151, paragraph 1, item (1), of the Civil Procedure Law of the PRC (for Trial Implementation), the court rendered judgment: dismissing the appeal and affirming the original judgment.
